name: Genetic Non-Syndromic Obesity

criteria.description: Severe obesity onset before 5 years of age
Positive family history of obesity consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance
Identification of pathogenic variant in obesity-related gene (e.g., MC4R, LEP, LEPR)
Lack of dysmorphic features or other syndromic manifestations
Exclusion of endocrine or environmental causes of obesity

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of early-onset severe obesity plus pathogenic genetic variant with exclusion of syndromic and secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential to confirm diagnosis; clinical features alone are insufficient.

pathognomonic.notes: Excessive appetite beginning in infancy or early childhood

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe obesity with BMI > 3 standard deviations above mean
pathognomonic.notes: Persistent and progressive weight gain despite normal activity

common.notes: Elevated insulin levels due to insulin resistance

common.symptomName: Increased adiposity predominantly in subcutaneous tissue
common.notes: Fat accumulation mainly in subcutaneous rather than visceral compartments

common.symptomName: Elevated leptin levels (except in leptin deficiency)
common.notes: Reflects leptin resistance in most cases

occasional.notes: May be present due to obesity-induced hormonal imbalance
searchTerms: female hormone disorder with cystic ovaries

occasional.symptomName: Mild hepatomegaly due to fatty infiltration
occasional.notes: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease secondary to obesity
searchTerms: small liver swelling due to fat

rare.notes: Rarely reported in some genetic forms

rare.symptomName: Psychiatric comorbidities including anxiety and depression
rare.notes: May develop secondary to chronic disease burden

rare.symptomName: Orthopedic complications such as slipped capital femoral epiphysis
rare.notes: Due to excessive weight and biomechanical stress
searchTerms: bone growth plate disorder in hip

laboratory: Elevated fasting insulin and glucose levels indicating insulin resistance
High leptin levels except in leptin deficiency mutations
Genetic testing revealing pathogenic variants in MC4R, LEP, LEPR, POMC genes
imaging: MRI or DEXA showing increased subcutaneous fat deposition
Liver ultrasound indicating fatty infiltration in some cases
genetic: Pathogenic variants in melanocortin 4 receptor gene (MC4R)
Leptin (LEP) or leptin receptor (LEPR) gene mutations
other: Absence of dysmorphic features or organ malformations

distinguishingFeatures: Elevated TSH and low free T4

redFlags: Onset of obesity with dysmorphic features or developmental delay
Severe hyperphagia unresponsive to behavioral interventions
Family history of syndromic obesity or multiple congenital anomalies
references: Farooqi IS, O'Rahilly S. Monogenic obesity in humans. Annu Rev Med. 2005;56:443-458.
Hinney A, et al. Genetics of obesity: what have we learned? Curr Opin Lipidol. 2010;21(1):3-9.
